author: Anshu Thakur
title: A Walmart Employee Accused a Woman of Not Paying for Her Steak, and She Was Detained Until Police Arrived. She Says She'd Already Scanned It - NewsBreak
text:
By Anshu Thakur ,
19 hours ago Image by JeepersMedia, CC BY 2.0. & TikTok/@thatssokeezy A Florida shopper says she was detained at Walmart over a piece of steak she says she had already paid for. According to Daily Dot , a store employee gave her a $1,000 gift card afterward to make up for the “embarrassment.” TikToker @thatssokeezy said she was doing a normal grocery run when she reached the self-checkout counter. She says a woman approached her partway through and accused her of not scanning her steak.
According to her account, she denied it, and a video on the checkout screen appeared to show her scanning the item . The employee still went through her bags item by item before apologizing and walking away. She says she finished checking out, paid, and headed for the exit, only to be stopped by multiple employees speaking into walkie-talkies. One of them asked for her receipt, then searched through her bags and brought up the steak again, telling her she hadn’t paid for it.
She says she explained that the earlier employee had already confirmed the scan, but the situation escalated. She was asked to step into what she described as a detainment room, and refused, saying she believed she hadn’t done anything wrong. An employee then threatened to call the sheriff’s office, according to her account.
The gift card wasn’t the only legal question this raised Police arrived within five minutes, she says. Officers asked her to step into the room to talk, saying they didn’t want to embarrass her in public. “Y’all are causing a big embarrassment over someone who’s innocent,” she told them, though she agreed to go inside rather than risk arrest. Once inside, officers went through everything on her receipt and began rescanning it.
@thatssokeezy they really detained me over a steak… SStorytimeFFunnyStoryStoreDrama
♬ original sound – ThatsSoKeezy | ? The store manager later stepped in and offered her a $1,000 gift card, which she accepted. Daily Dot noted several parts of the story remain unconfirmed on its end: the claimed scanner malfunction, the store’s version of the detention, and the specific terms of the gift card deal. Walmart had not made any public comment as of publication.
Whether a store could legally do this, if her account is accurate, comes down to a specific Florida law. Under Florida Statute 812.015 , a merchant or employee can detain someone suspected of retail theft without facing civil liability for false imprisonment. That protection only applies if they have probable cause, the detention is carried out in a reasonable manner, and law enforcement is called immediately afterward.
If the scan had genuinely already been confirmed before the detention continued, as she describes, that’s the kind of fact pattern that can undercut a merchant’s legal protection, since the statute’s immunity depends on probable cause existing at the time of detention, not on a suspicion that had already been cleared. That analysis rests entirely on her version of events, which, as noted above, hasn’t been independently confirmed.
Florida courts have found that a merchant loses the statute’s protection once probable cause is gone. That opens the door to a false imprisonment claim. This is separate from Florida’s civil theft statute, Section 772.11 . Stores themselves often use that law to send demand letters to suspected shoplifters, seeking up to three times the value of the item, plus a minimum of $200.
